children.text:
Mastering diagnostic tests and hospital services:

• *Pathology & Imaging:* When your GP gives you a referral for blood tests or X-rays, choose an approved provider network for direct billing.

• *Hospital Admissions:* If you need overnight care, public hospitals provide comprehensive care covered by OSHC. Contact your insurer promptly to issue a guarantee of payment.

• *Digital Records:* Keep your eScripts, specialist referrals, and immunisation history saved on your phone for easy access across Australian clinics.
A doctor examines you and recommends a blood test and an ankle X-ray. How do diagnostic pathology and imaging services generally work under the Australian healthcare system?

data-source.title: Option A
data-source.description: The GP gives you a referral form to take to an accredited pathology or imaging clinic

data-source.title: Option B
data-source.description: You must personally purchase blood testing machinery from a local pharmacy shop

data-source.title: Option C
data-source.description: Diagnostic scans can only be performed if you are admitted overnight to hospital

data-source.title: Option D
data-source.description: Blood tests are illegal for temporary international visa holders in Australia

children.text: You need planned medical treatment in a private hospital. Why is it advantageous to check whether the private hospital is in your insurer’s "Members’ Choice" network?

data-source.title: Option A
data-source.description: Members’ Choice hospitals have agreed rates that help reduce unexpected out-of-pocket costs

data-source.title: Option B
data-source.description: Non-network hospitals are completely free for all international university students

data-source.title: Option C
data-source.description: Members’ Choice hospitals allow patients to bypass Australian visa requirements

data-source.title: Option D
data-source.description: Choosing a network hospital guarantees that your semester grades will increase

children.text: You witness a severe traffic accident near your student campus and need to call for emergency paramedics. Do you need mobile credit or a local phone plan to dial 000 in Australia?

data-source.title: Option A
data-source.description: Yes, emergency calls require a minimum of $20 international calling credit

data-source.title: Option B
data-source.description: No, calls to 000 are completely free from any mobile phone, landline, or payphone

data-source.title: Option C
data-source.description: Yes, you must enter your student visa identification number before connecting

data-source.title: Option D
data-source.description: No, but you can only call 000 if your university campus security office is open

children.text: You attend a public hospital emergency department with a minor finger cut. Other patients who arrive after you with severe chest pain are seen first. Why does this occur?

data-source.title: Option A
data-source.description: Australian hospital emergency departments treat patients based on medical urgency (triage)

data-source.title: Option B
data-source.description: The hospital prioritizes patients based on how long their student visa lasts

data-source.title: Option C
data-source.description: International students are always placed at the end of the line regardless of symptoms

data-source.title: Option D
data-source.description: The receptionists only treat patients who hold private Australian citizenship cards

children.text: A student is prescribed specialized medication for a complex condition. The pharmacist explains that the medication is not subsidized by the government PBS for non-residents. What should the student understand about costs?

data-source.title: Option A
data-source.description: OSHC benefits for pharmaceuticals have set limits, meaning high-cost drugs can have large gaps

data-source.title: Option B
data-source.description: The Australian government pays 100% of all experimental treatments for foreign visitors

data-source.title: Option C
data-source.description: Private health insurers will automatically buy the pharmaceutical company on your behalf

data-source.title: Option D
data-source.description: The student must immediately renounce their visa to receive medication in Australia

children.text:
*Correct Answer:* Option A (The GP gives you a referral form to take to an accredited pathology or imaging clinic)

💡 *Explanation:* In Australia, doctors provide referral request forms for pathology (blood tests) or radiology (X-rays/ultrasounds), which you take to an accredited diagnostic clinic. OSHC contributes benefits towards included MBS diagnostic items.

🔗 *Source Reference:* [Medibank OSHC Member Guide](https://www.medibank.com.au/content/dam/b2c/docs/mpl/Medibank_OSHC_Member_Guide.pdf)
https://www.medibank.com.au/content/dam/b2c/docs/mpl/Medibank_OSHC_Member_Guide.pdf

*Correct Answer:* Option A (Members’ Choice hospitals have agreed rates that help reduce unexpected out-of-pocket costs)

💡 *Explanation:* Members’ Choice private hospitals have agreements with your health insurer establishing agreed pricing for hospital accommodation and theatre fees, minimizing out-of-pocket gap expenses. Non-network private hospitals may result in significantly higher out-of-pocket costs.

🔗 *Source Reference:* [Medibank OSHC Member Guide](https://www.medibank.com.au/content/dam/b2c/docs/mpl/Medibank_OSHC_Member_Guide.pdf)
https://www.medibank.com.au/content/dam/b2c/docs/mpl/Medibank_OSHC_Member_Guide.pdf

*Correct Answer:* Option B (No, calls to 000 are completely free from any mobile phone, landline, or payphone)

💡 *Explanation:* In Australia, calls to 000 (Triple Zero) are free of charge from any telephone, including mobile phones without credit, SIM cards, or landlines.

🔗 *Source Reference:* [What you need to know about the Australian healthcare system](https://www.medibank.com.au/overseas-health-insurance/guides/articles/understanding-australian-healthcare/)
https://www.medibank.com.au/overseas-health-insurance/guides/articles/understanding-australian-healthcare/

*Correct Answer:* Option A (Australian hospital emergency departments treat patients based on medical urgency (triage))

💡 *Explanation:* Australian emergency departments operate on clinical triage, meaning patients with critical or life-threatening conditions are always treated first. Non-urgent cases may experience long waiting times, which is why a GP or urgent care clinic is often more appropriate for minor issues.

🔗 *Source Reference:* [The Australian Healthcare System | Overseas health insurance | Medibank](https://www.medibank.com.au/overseas-health-insurance/guides/australian-healthcare/)
https://www.medibank.com.au/overseas-health-insurance/guides/australian-healthcare/

*Correct Answer:* Option A (OSHC benefits for pharmaceuticals have set limits, meaning high-cost drugs can have large gaps)

💡 *Explanation:* Because international students are generally not eligible for PBS government subsidies, high-cost medicines can be expensive. OSHC policies have annual pharmaceutical benefit limits, which may result in significant out-of-pocket expenses.

🔗 *Source Reference:* [Medibank OSHC Member Guide](https://www.medibank.com.au/content/dam/b2c/docs/mpl/Medibank_OSHC_Member_Guide.pdf)
https://www.medibank.com.au/content/dam/b2c/docs/mpl/Medibank_OSHC_Member_Guide.pdf

• *Healthdirect Hotline:* 1800 022 222 (24/7 Registered Nurse advice)
• *Emergency Services:* 000 (Ambulance, Fire, Police - life threats only)
• *National Home Doctor:* 13 74 25 (After-hours bulk-billed home visits)
